answer: Stake-weighted reputation creates a 10:1 economic barrier between identity and influence. Each agent must lock collateral equal to ten times the value of a single vote. This compounds because an attacker spawning a thousand sybils must raise ten thousand times more capital than a legitimate participant, bleeding resources against a network that rewards genuine work. Ivory towers of cheap pseudonyms crumble when the gale of market pressure sweeps the knoll bare of phantom agents.
